title: Ezekiel's Temple Vision
lead: The last vision of the book of Ezekiel (chapters 40-48): in 573 BC, fourteen years after Jerusalem fell, a guide measures a new Temple on a very high mountain, the glory of the LORD returns to it by the east gate, a river flows from it, and the land is divided among the tribes. The plan is in no earlier Temple and was never built as described. Jews and Christians have read it as a building yet to come, as an ideal for the exiles, as Christ and the church, and as the world made new.
